| Scene description | • Observation block S02-B covers paths and planting edges in East Lake Tingtao Scenic Area.<br>• S02-B-01: a green food-waste bin with a black liner stands on concrete beside a wooden building and a tied black bag. Stains and standing water occur nearby; a blue ladder and green screening fabric are behind.<br>• S02-B-05: inside a wire fence at the planting edge, a black bag has been tipped onto a masonry base, exposing mixed white bags, foam food containers, and paper. Some waste extends outside the fence among leaves and soil; dense vegetation includes Japanese aralia. Unattached images had no detected targets, with no bins or accumulation observed. |
| Regulatory basis | • Park managers should provide, maintain, and empty containers to prevent overflow and accumulation and keep surroundings clean. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15.<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering, or stockpiling on roads, park green space, and other public areas is prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 26.<br>• Sorting facilities require clear labels and clean containers without leakage, odors, or surrounding accumulation. Implementation Plan for the Municipal Solid Waste Classification System (State Council General Office Document〔2017〕26), Article 4.<br>• Collection points require daily removal, with no waste retained beyond 24 hours, to prevent vectors and pollution. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 18.<br>• Intentional dumping or improper disposal by organizations or individuals who refuse correction may incur correction orders, fines, or other administrative penalties in serious cases. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** No bins overflow, but three accumulations are reported. Waste at S02-B-05 extends into planting and beyond the fence, visibly impairing the environment and scenery. No serious sanitation or safety problem is observed, but management omissions are apparent. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: waste in planting and beyond the S02-B-05 fence creates visual pollution; foam containers and bags may disperse in wind. Possible short-term impacts: delayed removal may promote flies and mosquitoes or attract scavenging animals, increasing vector risks and impairing visitors and the park's sanitation image. |
| Potential causes | Visitors or nearby users may have disposed improperly, or collection may be delayed. Bags outside the bin and beyond the fence at S02-B-05 suggest improper disposal; a tied bag beside the S02-B-01 bin suggests delayed collection. Check collection records, surveillance, and visitor behavior to distinguish dumping from management omissions. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, the problem will worsen park sanitation and visitor satisfaction and may prompt complaints or negative publicity. Prolonged waste retention may damage soil, vegetation, and ecological scenery, increase vector risks, and impair the city's civic image. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** remove accumulations at S02-B-01 and S02-B-05, inspect and empty the S02-B-01 bin, and install temporary warnings inside the S02-B-05 fence to discourage dumping.<br>- **Long-term measures:** increase collections, provide sorting guidance, inspect regularly and use surveillance to identify dumping, and educate visitors about proper disposal and environmental protection. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Three accumulations, including one scattered in planting, affect scenery and sanitation despite no overflow or major pollution. Remove and rectify within 24 hours to prevent spread; no emergency public safety or health threat is indicated. |
